articles.title: How do I give my LLM workflow persistent context across independent client connections?
articles.excerpt: You build a support workflow in two steps. At 06:00 a scheduled job connects to your MCP server, reads the night's tickets and works out that 4127 and 4133 are the same bug. At 10:00 you open a chat c…
articles.body: You build a support workflow in two steps. At 06:00 a scheduled job connects to your MCP server, reads the night's tickets and works out that 4127 and 4133 are the same bug. At 10:00 you open a chat client and ask the agent which tickets can be closed. That is a new client connection, perhaps to a different server instance, and the agent starts from nothing. What the first step worked out lived with the first connection, and that connection closed four hours ago. The short answer: do not key the context by the connection. Store it outside the server process, under the stable identity it belongs to, such as the user, the project or the agent, and have every connection authenticate as that identity and read the context before it acts.

articles.title: Let's Not Be Hangry: An Open-Model App for My Boyfriend, Who Forgets to Eat
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend My boyfriend has been staying with me while I recover from ankle surgery. He's been taking care of me, and I noticed he…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend What I Built My boyfriend has been staying with me while I recover from ankle surgery. He's been taking care of me, and I noticed he wasn't taking care of himself. He forgets to eat. When he's busy, lunch just doesn't happen. And because it's my kitchen, he's hesitant to help himself to anything. So I built Let's Not Be Hangry , a tiny app with one job: make eating faster and easier than skipping. "How much time you got?" He taps 1 min , 5 min or 15 min , and Gemma picks something from my kitchen that fits, tells him exactly where it is ("freezer door"), and how to eat it. No-cooking options come first. A "fair game" list. I filled it with everything he's welcome to. If it's on the list, it's his.

articles.title: Architecting reliable geofencing in Android without battery suicide
articles.excerpt: The awkward silence It happened during a quiet afternoon in the local library. I was sitting in a study room with three other developers, and the silence was heavy. Suddenly, my phone erupted into a r…
articles.body: The awkward silence It happened during a quiet afternoon in the local library. I was sitting in a study room with three other developers, and the silence was heavy. Suddenly, my phone erupted into a ringtone I thought I had disabled. It wasn't just a buzz; it was a loud, aggressive notification sound that seemed to echo off the walls. I fumbled to silence it, but the delay was enough. Everyone stared. In that moment, the productivity of the entire group evaporated, replaced by the universal, burning shame of being the person whose phone interrupted the workflow. The friction of manual management We live in a world of high-context environments. I need my phone silenced when I enter the office, when I’m at the mosque for prayer, or when I’m in a focused coding session.

articles.excerpt: Tom Cruise's Digger bombed hard in theaters, pulling in an estimated $20 million in its opening weekend at the global box office.
articles.body: Tom Cruise's Digger bombed hard in theaters, pulling in an estimated $20 million in its opening weekend at the global box office. It's a crushing start for the Alejandro González Iñárritu-directed dark comedy. The movie, which stars an unrecognizable Cruise under a thick bed of makeup, accumulated just $8 million domestically and $12 million internationally. It's a $20 million total that props Digger up to be crushed under the weight of its $160 million production budget (via Deadline ). With marketing costs unclear, it signals a long, long line to walk if the movie wants to even sniff at turning a profit. "An oil tycoon faces a mounting environmental catastrophe as politicians and scientists struggle to contain the crisis," a description for Digger says.

Selfie at Vera Rubin Ridge Explanation: On sol 1943 of its journey of exploration across the surface of Mars, the Curiosity Rover recorded this selfie at the south rim of Vera Rubin Ridge. Of course a sol is a Martian solar day , about 40 minutes longer than an Earth day. Curiosity’s sol 1943 corresponds to Earth date January 23, 2018.

articles.title: NASA Astronaut Christina Koch to Join NFL Fans in Philadelphia
articles.excerpt: As part of NASA’s ongoing Inspiration Tour, NASA astronaut Christina Koch will highlight America’s strengths in space exploration and aeronautics innovation at the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Los Angeles…
articles.body: NASA astronaut Christina Koch is seen during an event to award the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the Artemis II crew, Friday, Aug. 28, 2026, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credit: NASA/John Kraus As part of NASA’s ongoing Inspiration Tour, NASA astronaut Christina Koch will highlight America’s strengths in space exploration and aeronautics innovation at the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Los Angeles Rams game in Philadelphia on Sunday, Oct. 4. A self-proclaimed Philadelphia sports fan, Koch is an explorer and engineer who spent a total of 338 days in space across two missions, including serving as a mission specialist for the agency’s Artemis II mission earlier this year.
